scope: G001 MCP daemon-backed tool execution final gate

securityReview.hardcodedSecrets: none found in the changed runtime or evidence files
securityReview.unsafeCode: tdw-app-client and tdw-mcp keep their existing forbid-unsafe posture; no unsafe blocks were introduced
securityReview.daemonBoundary: daemon-backed tools fail closed on invalid endpoints, unsupported transports, connection failures, malformed frames, oversized frames, timeout, or missing terminal events
securityReview.cleanRoom: clean-room audit passed; no finx-* crate/dependency, copied FinX-XR code, or tdw-provider-openbb dependency was introduced
securityReview.toolRisk: tdw.daemon.query.submit intentionally submits caller SQL as a non-read-only MCP tool through the daemon/service-api policy path; input is bounded and control-character checked

architectureReview.rationale: The daemon framing and submit-and-wait behavior live in tdw-app-client, while tdw-mcp remains an MCP surface that builds narrow protocol operations and formats terminal event evidence. Deterministic fixture tools stay offline, and daemon-backed tools use the existing tdw-app-server length-delimited protocol with an in-process TCP integration test.
watchItems: UDS and HTTP-SSE daemon client support remain a documented follow-up; this gate intentionally ships the local TCP default and explicit unsupported-transport fail-closed behavior.

transportReview.streamableHttp: streamable HTTP smoke passed after the daemon-backed tool changes
transportReview.daemonTcp: new daemon-backed MCP tools roundtrip against an in-process TCP daemon without Docker
